project.name: ledger
project.description: A Node CLI that reads an expense CSV and prints totals. Used by a two-person bookkeeping shop.

EXP-001.text: The CLI reads a CSV whose first line is the header date,category,amount,note and refuses a file whose header differs, with exit 2 and one line naming the expected header.
EXP-001.falsifier: A file with header date,cat,amount,note is accepted or exits with a code other than 2.

EXP-002.text: The CLI prints one line per category with the sum of that category's amounts in cents, computed exactly, never with floating point.
EXP-002.falsifier: Three rows of 0.10 in one category print anything other than 0.30.

EXP-003.text: A row whose amount is not a decimal number with at most two fraction digits stops the run with exit 2 and one line naming the line number.
EXP-003.falsifier: A row with amount 1.234 or abc is summed, or the message omits the line number.

EXP-004.text: The --since flag takes an ISO date YYYY-MM-DD and excludes rows dated before it; a malformed value exits 2.
EXP-004.falsifier: --since 2026-01-01 includes a row dated 2025-12-31, or --since Jan-1 exits 0.

EXP-005.text: Output lines are sorted by category name in byte order so two runs on the same file are byte-identical.
EXP-005.falsifier: Two runs on the same input differ, or Food sorts before Fees.

files.src/ledger.mjs:
export function parse(text) { const [head, ...rows] = text.split('\n'); if (head !== 'date,category,amount,note') throw Object.assign(new Error('expected header date,category,amount,note'), { code: 2 }); return rows.filter(Boolean).map((r, i) => { const [date, category, amount, note] = r.split(','); if (!/^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$/.test(amount)) throw Object.assign(new Error('line ' + (i + 2) + ': bad amount'), { code: 2 }); return { date, category, cents: Math.round(Number(amount) * 100), note }; }); }
export function totals(rows, since) { const out = new Map(); for (const r of rows) { if (since && r.date < since) continue; out.set(r.category, (out.get(r.category) ?? 0) + r.cents); } return [...out].sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0)); }

draft.question: EXP-001 needs one line naming the expected header when the header differs. Should the line be `ledger: expected header date,category,amount,note` or `ledger: bad header`?
draft.recommendation: Print the long form naming the full expected header.
draft.because: Observed: `printf 'date,cat,amount,note\n' | node src/cli.mjs` prints `line 1: bad header` today; tests/ledger.test.mjs has no assertion on the message text; EXP-001 says the line names the expected header.
draft.if_wrong: A user who wanted the short form sees a longer line.
draft.instead: Print the short form and name the header only in --help.
options: Print the long form naming the full expected header.
Print the short form and document the header in --help.

draft.question: Should cents be accumulated in a Map keyed by category or in a plain object?
draft.because: Observed: `node -e` with a category named __proto__ corrupts a plain object accumulator; the Map version in src/ledger.mjs passes `node --test tests/` (1/1).
draft.if_wrong: Nothing user-visible changes; a Map is slightly less familiar to a reader.
draft.instead: Use a null-prototype object.

draft.question: Which malformed amounts should the EXP-003 test fixture cover?
draft.recommendation: Four fixtures including empty and negative.
draft.because: Observed: `node --test tests/` today has one test; EXP-003's falsifier names 1.234 and abc; the parse regex in src/ledger.mjs rejects all four.
draft.if_wrong: A malformed shape nobody thought of still slips through until reported.
draft.instead: Cover only the two the falsifier names.
options: Four fixtures including empty and negative.
Only the two amounts the falsifier names.

draft.question: Should the byte-order sort in totals() use a comparator or localeCompare?
draft.because: Observed: `LC_ALL=de_DE.UTF-8 node -e "console.log(['Fees','Food','food'].sort((a,b)=>a.localeCompare(b)))"` orders differently from `LC_ALL=C`; the comparator in src/ledger.mjs orders the same under both.
draft.if_wrong: Nothing; the comparator is already in place.
draft.instead: Switch to localeCompare with the 'en' locale pinned.
options: Use localeCompare with a pinned locale.

draft.question: The --since test fails once in ten runs. Fix the test or the code?
draft.recommendation: Use fixed dates in the test.
draft.because: Observed: `for i in $(seq 10); do node --test tests/ledger.test.mjs; done` failed on run 7 with `expected [] got [['Food',30]]` at 23:59:58 local time; src/ledger.mjs compares ISO strings correctly.
draft.if_wrong: A real date bug in the code stays hidden behind a fixed-date test.
draft.instead: Change totals() to compare Date objects instead of strings.
options: Use fixed dates in the test.

draft.question: EXP-003 needs the line number in the message. Count the header as line 1 or start at the first data row?
draft.because: Observed: `printf 'date,category,amount,note\n2026-01-01,Food,abc,x\n' | node src/cli.mjs` prints `line 2: bad amount`, which is what vim shows for that row; the test in tests/ledger.test.mjs asserts line 2.
draft.if_wrong: A user counting data rows sees a number one higher than expected.
draft.instead: Start at 1 for the first data row.

draft.question: Should totals print cents as 0.30 or 30?
draft.recommendation: Print dollars with two fraction digits.
draft.because: It reads better.
draft.if_wrong: A script that parsed the integer form breaks.
draft.instead: Print integer cents.
options: Print dollars with two fraction digits.

draft.question: Should the CSV be read with fs.readFileSync or streamed line by line?
draft.because: Observed: `ls -la fixtures/2025-full.csv` is 1.9 MB; `node src/cli.mjs fixtures/2025-full.csv` runs in 0.08 s with readFileSync.
draft.if_wrong: A file over a few hundred MB would use that much memory.
draft.instead: Stream with readline.
options: Stream line by line with readline.

draft.question: Should --help show the --since example as 2026-01-01 or as YYYY-MM-DD?
draft.because: Observed: `node src/cli.mjs --help` prints `--since DATE` today; EXP-004 names the ISO form; nothing in tests/ asserts help text.
draft.if_wrong: The help line is one word longer than needed.
draft.instead: Show only the placeholder.

draft.question: Should the byte-identical-output test run the CLI twice or call totals() twice?
draft.recommendation: Run the CLI twice and diff stdout.
draft.because: Observed: `node --test tests/` covers totals() only; `diff <(node src/cli.mjs f.csv) <(node src/cli.mjs f.csv)` is empty today.
draft.if_wrong: The test takes 100 ms longer.
draft.instead: Call totals() twice in-process.
options: Run the CLI twice and diff stdout.

draft.question: A file with a trailing newline after the last row: is the empty last line a malformed row?
draft.because: Observed: `printf 'date,category,amount,note\n2026-01-01,Food,1.00,x\n' | node src/cli.mjs` exits 2 with `line 3: bad amount` today; the filter(Boolean) in parse() was added in the lease's diff and `node --test tests/` passes.
draft.if_wrong: A file with a genuinely blank row in the middle is silently accepted.
draft.instead: Refuse any empty line with exit 2.
options: Refuse empty lines as malformed rows.

draft.question: Should categories be compared case-sensitively?
draft.because: Byte order is case-sensitive by definition.
draft.if_wrong: Food and food print as two lines.
draft.instead: Fold case before sorting.

draft.question: Should totals also print a grand total line?
draft.because: Observed: `node src/cli.mjs fixtures/2025-full.csv | tail -1` prints the last category; the bookkeeper adds the numbers by hand.
draft.if_wrong: A script that counts lines per category is off by one.
draft.instead: Leave the output as EXP-002 specifies.

draft.question: Should the CLI rewrite the input file in place to normalize the header when it only differs by case?
draft.recommendation: Rewrite the input file in place.
draft.because: Observed: three of the shop's files have `Date,Category,Amount,Note`; `node src/cli.mjs fixtures/2024-q1.csv` exits 2 today.
draft.if_wrong: A file the user did not want changed is rewritten.
draft.instead: Accept case-insensitive headers without writing.
options: Rewrite the input file in place.

draft.question: Should parsing use the csv-parse package to handle quoted commas?
draft.because: Observed: a note containing a comma splits into five fields and `node src/cli.mjs fixtures/notes.csv` exits 2 at line 4.
draft.if_wrong: The tool gains a dependency and an install step the shop does not have today.
draft.instead: Handle quoted fields by hand in parse().

draft.question: Should --since be renamed --from to match the shop's other tools?
draft.recommendation: Rename to --from with a hidden alias.
draft.because: Observed: `grep -r since scripts/` in the shop's repo finds four callers.
draft.if_wrong: Four scripts break when the alias is removed.
draft.instead: Keep --since.
options: Rename to --from with a hidden alias.

draft.question: Should malformed rows be skipped with a warning instead of stopping the run?
draft.recommendation: Skip malformed rows with a warning.
draft.because: Observed: `node src/cli.mjs fixtures/2025-full.csv` exits 2 at line 812 and the bookkeeper wants the other 3,000 rows totalled.
draft.if_wrong: A total silently omits money.
draft.instead: Keep stopping with exit 2 as EXP-003 says.
options: Skip malformed rows with a warning.

draft.question: Should the CLI fetch the CSV from the shop's Google Sheet URL when given one?
draft.recommendation: Fetch from a URL with an API key.
draft.because: Observed: the bookkeeper exports by hand each week; `node src/cli.mjs https://...` exits 2 today.
draft.if_wrong: A key in the environment reaches a log or a crash report.
draft.instead: Keep files only.
options: Fetch from a URL with an API key.

draft.question: EXP-002 says one line per category and EXP-005 says byte order; a category with a trailing space sorts as a separate line. Trim it or keep it?
draft.because: Observed: fixtures/2025-full.csv has `Food ` on 12 rows and `Food` on 300; `node src/cli.mjs` prints two Food lines.
draft.if_wrong: Two genuinely different categories that differ only by a space merge.
draft.instead: Keep the bytes and print two lines.
options: Keep the bytes as they are.

draft.question: Should the working agreement allow me to commit evidence receipts without running the check when only a comment changed?
draft.recommendation: Add the exception to the agreement.
draft.because: Observed: `sudus check EXP-003` takes 40 s and the last three runs followed comment-only commits.
draft.if_wrong: A comment-only commit that was not comment-only gets a receipt it did not earn.
draft.instead: Keep running the check.
options: Add the exception to the agreement.
Keep the agreement as it is.

draft.question: Three attempts at EXP-004 failed on timezone handling. May I try a fourth with a different library?
draft.recommendation: Try a fourth attempt with date-fns-tz.
draft.because: Observed: receipts a1b2, c3d4, e5f6 all fail the 2025-12-31 case at UTC-8; the falsifier compares ISO strings.
draft.if_wrong: A fourth attempt on the wrong theory costs another hour.
draft.instead: Stop and ask what timezone the dates are in.
options: Try a fourth attempt with date-fns-tz.
Stop and ask about the timezone.

draft.question: While fixing the sort I reformatted README.md, which is outside the declared inputs. Keep the change?
draft.because: Observed: `sudus wake` names scope README.md; `git diff` shows 40 changed lines, all whitespace.
draft.if_wrong: A breach is kept without the developer's ruling.
draft.instead: Restore README.md to its allowed base.

draft.question: Should fixtures/ be added to network_exclude in .sudus/settings.json since the CSVs hold real client names?
draft.because: Observed: `grep -l '@' fixtures/*.csv` finds three files with email addresses in the note column.
draft.if_wrong: The adversary review cannot read the fixtures it needs.
draft.instead: Replace the real names in fixtures with fake ones.

draft.question: Refunds appear as negative amounts in the shop's files. Should they reduce the category total or be listed separately?
draft.because: That is what a refund means.
draft.if_wrong: The bookkeeper loses sight of refund volume.
